    Architecture - Enum Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.board
    The instruction set an ArduinoCore runs generated code on, which picks the code generator: the UNO R4's Cortex-M4 and the UNO Q's Cortex-M33 share one Thumb-2 backend, the UNO WiFi Rev2's ATmega4809 has its own AVR one, and the Nano ESP32's ESP32-S3 an Xtensa one.

    The Arduino UNO board's microcontroller unit (MCU): its Gpio pins, its I2c bus, its USB Mouse, its built-in LedMatrix, its onboard Wifi, its Clock, which board it is (BoardModel) and its arena and flash figures (BoardMemory).

    ArduinoUnoQBoard - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.annotations
    Selects the Arduino UNO Q as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its STM32U585 microcontroller (Cortex-M33) under Arduino's Zephyr core.
    ArduinoUnoR3Board - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.annotations
    Selects the classic Arduino UNO R3 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ATmega328P, an 8-bit AVR with 2 KB SRAM and 32 KB flash, under Arduino's arduino:avr core.
    ArduinoUnoR3WiFiRev2Board - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.annotations
    Selects the Arduino UNO WiFi Rev2 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ATmega4809, an 8-bit megaAVR (6 KB SRAM, 48 KB flash), under Arduino's arduino:megaavr core, with Wi-Fi through the u-blox NINA-W102 module and the WiFiNINA library.
    ArduinoUnoR4WiFiBoard - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.annotations
    Selects the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi as @Board's target; has the onboard 12x8 LED matrix.
    ArduinoWifiShield - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.wifi
    The retired Arduino WiFi Shield, the UNO R3's only way onto a Wi-Fi network: the R3 has no radio of its own, so ArduinoUno.getWifi() is rejected there and the program takes its Wifi from this shield instead.

    AVR_ARENA_CAPACITY_BYTES - Static variable in class io.github.jabrena.juno.RuntimeLimits
    The arena of an AVR board (the UNO WiFi Rev2's ATmega4809 has 6 KB of RAM in all) when the build sets none; RuntimeLimits.AVR_MAX_ARENA_BYTES is the most it accepts, leaving the rest for the stack, the core and its libraries.

    AVR_THREAD_STACK_BYTES - Static variable in class io.github.jabrena.juno.RuntimeLimits
    Stack bytes of each extra task on an AVR board (the UNO WiFi Rev2's 6 KB of RAM), and the most juno.Xss may ask for there.
    AvrAsmBackend - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.avr
    Emits GNU AVR assembly (avrxmega3, the UNO WiFi Rev2's ATmega4809) straight from Juno IR — the 8-bit counterpart of Thumb2AsmBackend, with the same storage model: every IR value and JVM local lives in a fixed stack slot (see FrameLayout.packed(IrMethod)) and registers are only scratch within one instruction, so a method can never run out of registers.

    avrPort(int, int) - Method in class io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime.ThreadRuntime

    AvrShimThunks - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime
    Generates the C++ thunks AVR code calls the runtime shim through. avr-gcc passes a const char* in two registers, an int32_t in four and a uint8_t in one, so assembly that only knows Java words cannot call a C function directly without knowing its parameter types.

    io.github.jabrena.juno - package io.github.jabrena.juno
    Juno's top-level compiler entry points: the CLI, the embeddable compiler API, and the small value types that connect them.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.analysis - package io.github.jabrena.juno.analysis
    Control-flow structure and conservative resource/runtime-risk analysis over decoded bytecode.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.annotations - package io.github.jabrena.juno.annotations
    Compile-time-only annotations an entry-point class uses to configure Juno's compilation, read directly from the class file rather than at runtime.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
    Code generation: turns optimized Juno IR into a complete Arduino sketch, generated assembly plus the C++ runtime shim it links against, for every supported board.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.avr - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.avr
    The AVR code generator: AvrAsmBackend emits avr-gcc assembly for the ATmega4809 UNO WiFi Rev2, calling the runtime shim through generated word-interface thunks.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime
    The C++ runtime shim the generated assembly links against: the arena allocator and collector, Serial, threads, and every optional library binding a program's ShimFeatures call for.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime.core - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime.core
    One CoreRuntime per ArduinoCore: every board-to-core difference lives in exactly one implementation here.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime.spi - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime.spi
    The contracts between the code generators and the runtime shim: ShimFeature, the optional shim parts generated code asks for, and CoreRuntime, which each Arduino core implements in backend.runtime.core.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.thumb2 - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.thumb2
    The Thumb-2 code generator: Thumb2AsmBackend emits GNU ARM Thumb-2 assembly for the Cortex-M4 UNO R4 WiFi and the Cortex-M33 UNO Q, one generator for both cores.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.xtensa - package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.xtensa
    The Xtensa code generator: XtensaAsmBackend emits GNU Xtensa assembly for the Nano ESP32's ESP32-S3, calling the runtime shim directly through the windowed-register ABI.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.board - package io.github.jabrena.juno.board
    Juno's model of a compilation target: Board, resolved from the entry-point class's @Board annotation (see Board) via Board.fromApiClassName(String), or the explicitly requested board when the entry point carries no annotation.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.bytecode - package io.github.jabrena.juno.bytecode
    Decodes the intentionally small JVM bytecode subset Juno v0.1 supports.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.classfile - package io.github.jabrena.juno.classfile
    Reads standard JVM class files and resolves their constant-pool references, independent of Juno's own bytecode subset or IR.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware
    The board's own hardware and program-wide introspection: ArduinoUno and ArduinoNano hand out the board's pins, I2C bus, USB mouse, LED matrix, clock, BoardModel (which board the program was compiled for) and BoardMemory (Juno's arena and the program's flash usage).
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.audio - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.audio
     
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.carrier - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.carrier
    Pin maps for passive carrier boards a Nano plugs into, currently NanoConnectorCarrier: its microSD slot, Grove and Qwiic connectors are ordinary Nano header pins, so a carrier needs no compiler intrinsic of its own.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.grove - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.grove
    Zero-allocation drivers and pin names for peripherals connected through the Grove Base Shield.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.grove.sensors - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.grove.sensors
    Allocation-free Grove sensor drivers for digital, analog, I2C and infrared modules connected through the GroveBaseShield pin map.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.imu - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.imu
    Motion sensing: NineAxisMotionShield, the orientation sensor of the Arduino 9 Axis Motion Shield, over I2c.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.ir - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.ir
    Infrared serial transport: Infrared bit-bangs framed bytes over a 38 kHz IR receiver module and an IR LED on plain pins.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.ir.hx - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.ir.hx
    HX-53 emitter and HX-M121 receiver implementations of Juno's infrared transport interfaces.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.kasa - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.kasa
    Allocation-free local-network control of legacy TP-Link Kasa HS100 and HS110 smart plugs.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.lcd - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.lcd
    Drivers for character LCD shields, currently LcdKeypadShield: a 16x2 HD44780-compatible display in 4-bit mode plus 5 buttons read from a single resistor-ladder analog pin, wired for the shield's standard pinout.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.sd - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.sd
    SPI SD-card access: SdCard, taken from the shield that holds the card's socket (such as the DataLoggerShield), opens files through an InputStream accepted by Juno's bounded intrinsic implementation of Properties.load(java.io.InputStream).
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.servo - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.servo
    Motor handles: Servo drives a standard 3-wire hobby servo through the Arduino Servo library, and PwmServoShield drives up to sixteen of them from a PCA9685 servo shield over I2C.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.tft - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.tft
    Drivers for TFT display shields, currently TftTouchShield: the ELEGOO 2.8" 240x320 ILI9341 display on an 8-bit parallel bus, with a resistive touch panel and a microSD socket (its card is TftTouchShield.getSdCard()).
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.wifi - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.wifi
    Wi-Fi shields, currently ArduinoWifiShield: the retired Arduino WiFi Shield, which gives the UNO R3 the Wifi it has no radio for.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.display - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.display
     
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.drive - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.drive
    Board-independent motion coordination.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.gpio - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.gpio
    General-purpose digital/analog I/O: Gpio, the raw pin-number operations (pinMode/digitalWrite/digitalRead/ analogRead/analogWrite/toggle), and DigitalOutput, a zero-cost handle bound to one output pin (high/low/toggle/isHigh) for callers that prefer an object-shaped API over passing a pin number to every call.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.hid - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.hid
    USB HID mouse control: Mouse, which ArduinoUno.getMouse() hands out, backed by the Arduino Mouse library.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.i2c - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.i2c
    I2C register access: I2c reads and writes the registers of a peripheral on the board's primary I2C bus.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.imu - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.imu
    Device-independent inertial sensing contracts.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.internal - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.internal
    The board's native implementations: the classes whose methods are compiler intrinsics.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.keyboard - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.keyboard
     
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.led - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.led
    The built-in LED matrix of the UNO R4 WiFi (12x8) and the UNO Q (13x8): LedMatrix, the raw begin/loadFrame/clear operations that ArduinoUno.getLedMatrix() hands out, and LedCanvas, a boolean[HEIGHT][MAX_WIDTH] pixel buffer with shape and text drawing helpers that render into it and send it to the board's matrix with show.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.motor - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.motor
    Board-independent motor contracts.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net
    Wi-Fi connectivity for the UNO R4 WiFi, UNO Q, UNO WiFi Rev2 and the UNO R3 with the Arduino WiFi Shield: Wifi connects and reads the board's address.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.email - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.email
    Basic SMTP send / POP3S read built on Wifi's connection: Smtp to send a plain-text message to one recipient, and Pop3Client to report the mailbox message count and read the newest message's From/Subject and a bounded plain-text body into caller-owned buffers.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.http - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.http
    HTTP(S) client and server support built on Wifi's connection: HttpClient to send http:// and https:// requests into a caller-owned byte[] response buffer, Json to read typed values directly out of a response buffer without building a parsed document, and HttpServer (plain HTTP only) to serve requests, with HttpMethod/HttpStatus as named constants for both directions.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.tcp - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.tcp
    TCP over the board's Wi-Fi: Tcp gives a program one allocation-free connection with exact-length reads, for application protocols layered on top of it.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.udp - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.udp
    UDP over the board's Wi-Fi: Udp gives a program one allocation-free socket for discovery broadcasts, datagrams to known peers and non-blocking receives, and SntpClock configures the SNTP server behind LocalDateTime.now(), which synchronizes on a socket of its own.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.power - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.power
    Battery and power-management APIs for supported boards.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.serial - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.serial
    USB serial output: Serial and its BaudRate constants.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.time - package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.time
    Time: Clock is the monotonic uptime clock, for measuring elapsed time without blocking.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.intrinsic - package io.github.jabrena.juno.intrinsic
    The closed catalog of hardware operations Juno understands, independent of any particular Java method signature or Arduino-side lowering.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.ir - package io.github.jabrena.juno.ir
    Juno's own intermediate representation: a non-SSA, block-structured form that lowering produces from JVM bytecode, optimize transforms, and backend consumes to generate assembly.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.linker - package io.github.jabrena.juno.linker
    Closed-world reachability: starting at main, follows every statically resolvable call, resolves hardware intrinsics, and rejects anything reachable that falls outside Juno's supported subset — before any code generation is attempted.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.lowering - package io.github.jabrena.juno.lowering
    Lowers linked, reachable JVM bytecode into Juno's IR.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.optimize - package io.github.jabrena.juno.optimize
    IR-to-IR optimization passes run between lowering and the backend.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.pf - package io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.pf
    LEGO Power Functions infrared remote control.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.poweredup - package io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.poweredup
    Remote control of LEGO Powered Up hubs over Bluetooth Low Energy, backed by the Arduino ArduinoBLE library.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.rcx - package io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.rcx
    LEGO Mindstorms RCX infrared remote control, brick commands, sensors, and firmware transfer.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.util - package io.github.jabrena.juno.util
    General-purpose utilities: Delay blocks for a number of milliseconds or microseconds, Random provides seeded, bounded pseudorandom numbers backed by Arduino's generator, and UuidCodec converts supported UUID values to and from caller-owned 16-byte network representations.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.util.image - package io.github.jabrena.juno.util.image
    Zero-allocation image renderers for the supported Arduino TFT shields.
    io.github.jabrena.juno.util.mvc - package io.github.jabrena.juno.util.mvc
    A small model-view-controller toolkit for multi-screen programs on a TFT touch shield.

    The Nano boards, which belong to no UNO generation: every BoardModel query is false there.
    NANO_ESP32 - Enum constant in enum class io.github.jabrena.juno.board.Board
    The ESP32-S3 Nano: GPIO, delays, USB serial, SPI SD cards, the onboard Wi-Fi of its NORA-W106 module (station and access-point modes, with UDP and SNTP), plain HTTP and HTTPS requests (checked against Mozilla's root certificates), an HTTP and HTTPS server on station Wi-Fi, email over implicit TLS and STARTTLS (SMTP and POP3), Bluetooth LE for PoweredUpHubRemote, the hardware random-number generator behind UUID.randomUUID(), java.math, the double-precision libm its newlib toolchain ships, structured concurrency over FreeRTOS tasks, and a USB HID mouse through the core's TinyUSB stack, sharing the USB port with the serial console; the other optional capabilities are not wired to its core yet.
    NanoConnectorCarrier - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.carrier
    Pin map for the passive Arduino Nano Connector Carrier (ASX00061): a microSD card slot on SPI, four Grove sockets and one Qwiic connector, all wired to ordinary Nano header pins.

    ProgramLayout - Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
    Whole-program storage decisions made before any code is emitted: arena object sizes and field offsets, mutable static fields' .bss symbols, and the .rodata symbols of string literals and compiler-generated constant int arrays — plus the data sections holding them.
    ProgramLayout(IrProgram) - Constructor for class io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.ProgramLayout
    An object's fields are exactly the ones some LoadField/StoreField in the whole program actually touches (there's no class-file field table available here, only the IR), laid out in FieldRef.displayName() order — sequential 4-byte int slots, since every field this backend has seen is one.
    ProgramLayout.DataDirectives - Record Class in io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
    The assembler directives a data section is written with: word emits 32-bit values (ARM's .word; AVR's .word is 16-bit, so it uses .long), align 4-byte-aligns, and bss switches to the zero-initialized section (AVR's assembler has no .bss shorthand).
